name: Coral bleaching
summary: No fifth global bleaching event declared by NOAA as of 22 Nov; El Niño heat raises the risk of one
state: NOAA says the fourth global coral bleaching event likely ended in 2025, and Coral Reef Watch has not declared a fifth since (NOAA). A Global Coral Reef Monitoring Network report said El Niño conditions could bring another event (bdnews24, 2 Nov). Searches on 22 Nov found no new global declaration or confirmed regional mass bleaching, so Normal holds with risk rising as the very strong El Niño persists.
for_you: Bleaching risk matters most to reef-dependent fisheries and tourism in the tropics. NOAA Coral Reef Watch publishes bleaching heat-stress alerts by region.
rubric_hit: No global bleaching event in progress (NOAA) = Normal

sources.title: NOAA NESDIS — World's fourth mass coral bleaching event likely ended in 2025

why: Reefs support a quarter of marine species and coastal economies; mass bleaching is a direct sign of ocean heat stress.
drivers: Marine heatwaves, El Niño, warming trend.

rubric.alert: Bleaching extent at record levels with active new alerts in the past month.
rubric.watch: Global bleaching event in progress, or regional mass bleaching.
rubric.normal: No global bleaching event in progress.
